title: Purview architecture policy
description: The authoritative project responsibility, naming and dependency policy. The architecture tests read this document. See the purview-architests skill.

$schema.description: Pointer to this schema, so an editor validates the file as it is written.

version.description: Schema version of this document. Increment when a change would break a reader that understood the previous shape. Version 2 removed the 'rules' object, whose flags were never consulted; use SkipRule, or a waiver, to opt out of a rule.

qualifiedNameSeparator.description: Separates the responsibility from its implementation qualifier, as in Persistence.SqlServer.

dependencyArrowMeaning.description: States what an arrow means, so compile-time references are not confused with runtime calls.

sourceRoots.description: Repo-relative folders holding the projects. Defaults to ["src"]. An empty array scans the repository root, which suits a flat layout. Getting this wrong finds no projects, which the graphDiscovery rule reports rather than passing every other rule vacuously.

responsibilities.description: The responsibility catalogue. A project name is <Responsibility>[.<Implementation>]; only the first segment is classified.

discouragedProjectNames.description: Names that describe a category rather than a responsibility, so nothing can be excluded from them.

assemblyRules.description: The type-level dependency check. It reuses each responsibility's mayDependOn and mustNotDependOn against the types a compiled assembly actually references, so a dependency that only arrives transitively or through a package is caught too.

enabled.description: Whether the type-level check runs. It reads compiled assemblies by metadata only, so it needs a build to have produced them.

assemblyRoots.description: Repo-relative folders to scan for assemblies. An empty array scans the test output directory, which already holds every project the test project references, directly or transitively.

assemblyGlobs.description: File globs matched under each assembly root.

waivers.description: Deliberate, reviewed departures. A waiver excuses the narrowest thing possible - usually the name - and mapsTo keeps the project classified so every dependency rule still applies.

projectNameSegment.description: A single PascalCase segment, with no dots: the responsibility, not a qualified project name.

aliases.description: Recognised alternative names. An established project using one of these is not renamed.

mayDependOn.description: Responsibilities this one may reference at compile time. An empty array means it depends on nothing.

mustNotDependOn.description: Responsibilities this one must never reference. Must not overlap mayDependOn.

forbiddenPackagePrefixes.description: NuGet identifier prefixes that must not appear in this responsibility, such as Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore in Core.

forbiddenFrameworkReferences.description: Framework reference prefixes that must not appear in this responsibility, such as Microsoft.AspNetCore.App in a portable layer.

siblingIndependence.description: When true, qualified implementations of this responsibility must not reference one another.

project.description: The project name the waiver applies to, exactly as it appears on disk.

mapsTo.description: The responsibility this project actually has. Keeps every dependency rule in force while excusing the name.

rules.description: The rule ids this waiver excuses. A waiver that excuses nothing does nothing, and an unknown id is reported by the waiverIntegrity rule.

reason.description: Why the departure is acceptable. A blanket suppression with no reason makes the policy unfalsifiable.
